turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I've done her obs. Weight's 78 kilos, blood pressure 128 over 82, pulse 58, and temperature 36.2.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ta. Have a seat. What's the problem?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Nothing much. I'm a bit tired, work's been flat out, and I'm not getting any younger.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's been exhausted since before Christmas, doctor. Six months. Asleep half the weekend.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): It's not six months. A couple of months, tops. I have a lie-in, I don't sleep the weekend away.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): So the fatigue sits somewhere between a couple of months and six. You feeling the cold?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, a bit, but the office air con is arctic.
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's in a jumper when it's thirty degrees. Been like that for months.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): That's stretching it. I've always run cold. It's not a thing.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weight up?
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's gone up a whole dress size. Her clothes don't fit.
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): A kilo or two from sitting at a desk. Not a dress size.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Constipated?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): A bit bound up, every second or third day. Nothing dramatic.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): A few months, same as the tiredness. I eat rubbish at work, that's all it is.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mood low?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): A bit flat. It's the job. I'm not depressed.
[SEG0019] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's snappy with me, and that's new this year.
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): I'm not snappy. I'm fine.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain or shortness of breath?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Neither.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Headaches? Hair falling out?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): No headaches. Hair's the same.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Periods still going?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): They stopped two years ago. And no, I'm not pregnant, before you ask.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thyroid problems in the family?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Mum was on thyroid tablets for years. She died a while back.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ever had your thyroid checked?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Years back. Borderline, they said. Nothing came of it.
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I was there. The GP said it was normal, not borderline. That was about five years ago.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Borderline is what I remember.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you taking?
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Nothing regular. I was on Ferro-Grad C, one a day, but I stopped it in March.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Why did you stop?
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): It upset my stomach, and the blood test was alright, so I binned them.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any thyroxine, or an antidepressant?
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): The GP wrote a script for thyroxine, a tiny dose. I never filled it. I don't do antidepressants.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies?
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): No. None.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke or drink?
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): Never smoked. One glass of wine on a Friday.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): And work?
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): Office manager at a freight yard. Long days. The car park machine ate my coins on the way in, which didn't exactly cheer me up.

[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm calling this a possible underactive thyroid until the bloods say otherwise. You've got tiredness, feeling cold, weight up, constipation and a flat mood, and your mum was on thyroid treatment. Stress or menopause could still be the whole story.
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): If you reckon. I still say it's work and getting older.

[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stay for bloods today: TSH, free T4, and a full blood count. Come back in a fortnight for the results either way. If the bowels get painful or you don't go for a week, come back sooner. Ease off blaming your age until the numbers are in.
[SEG0048] person_1 (NURSE): I'll take her across to pathology next door once you're finished.
